item.source_text: Anna wants to wash her hands, but she never washes them properly.

reference_translations.text: Anna vuole lavarsi le mani, ma non se le lava mai bene.
reference_translations.notes: Standard. Cluster 'se le' = reflexive si + DOP le (f.pl for le mani); vowel change si -> se before another clitic; pre-verb because 'lava' is finite.

reference_translations.text: Anna vuole lavarsi le mani, ma non se le lava mai per bene.

item.explanation: A reflexive verb can co-occur with a direct-object pronoun (the body part or possession being acted on). The reflexive plus DOP cluster undergoes a vowel change: 3sg reflexive si becomes se before another clitic, giving se + le for f.pl 'them (the hands)'. Stack: se + le + lava. The cluster sits pre-verb because lava is finite.

verb_form.future.formation.irregular.dou.label: Assimilated double-r stems: vorrò, verrò, terrò, rimarrò, berrò
verb_form.future.formation.irregular.dou.description: A group where the syncope produces a consonant cluster that assimilates to a double r: volere gives vorr- (vorrò, vorrai, vorrà, vorremo, vorrete, vorranno), venire gives verr-, tenere gives terr-, rimanere gives rimarr-, bere gives berr-. verb_form.gerundio.formation.progressive.label: Progressive
verb_form.gerundio.formation.progressive.description: The progressive construction: stare conjugated in the appropriate tense plus the invariable gerund. Present progressive (sto parlando) is A2 and the most frequent; the past progressive (stavo leggendo) is B1; future and conditional progressives (starò / starei leggendo) are B1-B2. The skill is the assembly: conjugate stare for the person and tense, then append the gerund. The stare conjugation itself is owned by the relevant tense tree (present, imperfect, future, conditional); this leaf tests putting the two together.

verb_form.gerundio.formation.regular_and.label: -are gerund
verb_form.gerundio.formation.regular_and.description: The -are class forms the gerund in -ando: parlare gives parlando, mangiare gives mangiando, lavorare gives lavorando. The gerund is invariable (no person or number endings), so this is purely stem + -ando.

Sono andato would commit the walking to a single past day, which clashes with the recurring frame.

verb_form.gerundio.formation.progressive.label: Progressive
verb_form.gerundio.formation.progressive.description: The progressive construction: stare conjugated in the appropriate tense plus the invariable gerund. Present progressive (sto parlando) is A2 and the most frequent; the past progressive (stavo leggendo) is B1; future and conditional progressives (starò / starei leggendo) are B1-B2. The skill is the assembly: conjugate stare for the person and tense, then append the gerund. The stare conjugation itself is owned by the relevant tense tree (present, imperfect, future, conditional); this leaf tests putting the two together.

reference_translations.text: Ieri mattina, mentre facevo la spesa, ho incontrato Marco al supermercato.
reference_translations.notes: Background clause fronted; common Italian word-order choice for narrative effect.

translation.reveal: to bump into / run into - incontrare (informally)
to do the shopping - fare la spesa

item.explanation: When a past event drops into an unfolding scene, Italian splits the tenses: passato prossimo for the event and imperfetto for the scene. The single bump-into is the event; the doing-the-shopping is the backdrop. The conjunction 'mentre' is a textbook cue for the imperfetto on the verb it governs.

reference_translations.notes: Both nouns take the s-impure/z form: lo, uno.

item.explanation: 'Lo studente ha uno zaino.' A noun starting s+consonant or z takes the impure-s forms of the article: definite lo and indefinite uno. So lo studente and uno zaino, never il studente / un zaino.

common_errors.text: Il studente ha un zaino.
common_errors.note: WRONG: s+consonant and z force lo/uno, not il/un.

request_body.raw: Lo studente ha uno zaino.

article.definite.forms.label: Choosing the definite form
article.definite.forms.description: The form depends on gender, number and the sound the noun starts with: lo/gli before s+consonant, z, gn, ps, x, y; l' before a vowel; il/i otherwise.
